title: Cancer in transition: discovery of tumor-intrinsic transcriptional programs shaping the immune and microenvironmental landscape.
authors: Spitschak, Alf; Casalegno Garduno, Rosaely; Putzer, Brigitte M
one_liner_zh: 该综述聚焦癌症生物标志物与肿瘤微环境，提及转录因子和AI整合框架，但未以蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模为核心，方法深度不足。
abstract: Cancer biomarker discovery has traditionally focused on individual molecular features; however, tumor behavior and therapeutic response are governed by integrated transcriptional and epigenetic programs that shape immune and microenvironmental states. Deciphering the determinants of metastatic evolution and the complexity of cancer ecosystems is imperative for designing novel preventive and targeted therapies. Tumor complexity, driven by intrinsic cellular heterogeneity and the dynamic plasticity of cancer cells in response to microenvironmental cues, complicates therapeutic strategies based solely on defined molecular or genetic traits. Consequently, there is an urgent need for reliable predictive biomarkers that reflect cancer vulnerabilities, indicate disease progression, or predict patient-specific therapeutic responses to enable truly individualized treatment strategies. Current biomarkers encompass genetic and epigenetic alterations, non-coding RNAs, epithelial-mesenchymal transition-, stemness-, and metastasis-associated transcription factors, as well as cellular components of the tumor microenvironment, including immune cell subsets and cancer-associated fibroblasts. In immuno-oncology, additional biomarkers such as tumor mutational burden, mismatch repair deficiency/microsatellite instability-high status, and PD-L1 expression are widely used for patient stratification. Importantly, the reversible nature of epigenetic modifications, aberrant transcription factor activity, and cell-intrinsic signaling alterations, together with dynamic interactions within the tumor microenvironment, profoundly influence cancer behavior and treatment outcomes. This review summarizes recent advances in cancer and immune-related biomarker research. It outlines a regulatory, systems-level framework that integrates tumor-intrinsic gene control programs with multi-omic, cellular, spatial, and AI-enabled biomarkers. This framework aims to capture tumor plasticity more effectively and advance precision oncology.
abstract_zh: 癌症生物标志物的发现传统上聚焦于单个分子特征；然而，肿瘤行为和治疗反应受整合的转录和表观遗传程序调控，这些程序塑造了免疫和微环境状态。解析转移演化的决定因素及癌症生态系统的复杂性，对于设计新型预防性和靶向治疗策略至关重要。肿瘤复杂性由内在细胞异质性和癌细胞响应微环境线索的动态可塑性驱动，这使得仅基于特定分子或遗传特征的治療策略复杂化。因此，迫切需要可靠的预测性生物标志物，以反映癌症脆弱性、指示疾病进展或预测患者特异性治疗反应，从而实现真正的个体化治疗策略。当前生物标志物涵盖遗传和表观遗传改变、非编码RNA、上皮-间质转化（epithelial-mesenchymal transition）、干性和转移相关转录因子，以及肿瘤微环境的细胞组分，包括免疫细胞亚群和癌症相关成纤维细胞。在免疫肿瘤学中，额外生物标志物如肿瘤突变负荷、错配修复缺陷/微卫星不稳定性高状态及PD-L1表达被广泛用于患者分层。重要的是，表观遗传修饰的可逆性、异常转录因子活性和细胞内在信号改变，连同肿瘤微环境内的动态相互作用，深刻影响癌症行为和治疗结果。本综述总结了癌症和免疫相关生物标志物研究的最新进展，并概述了一个调控性、系统层面的框架，该框架将肿瘤内在基因控制程序与多组学、细胞、空间及人工智能驱动的生物标志物相结合。此框架旨在更有效地捕捉肿瘤可塑性并推进精准肿瘤学。
